architecture.mechanism: Three-arm differential observability with a witness-ratio guard distinguishes reversible concentration polarization from irreversible mineral scaling and biofouling on RO membranes, restoring Rank-2 Fisher observability and cutting estimation error by over 89%.
architecture.intervention: Retrofit the existing 2-arm differential RO cartridge array to a 3-arm configuration, deploy the witness-ratio guard (τref = |rref(t) − rref,0|/rref,0 > 0.03) as a runtime software invariant on the soft-sensor diagnostic pipeline, and harden all production classes to remove simulator oracle access, thereby enabling earlier and unambiguous biofilm-onset identification separate from CP and scaling signals.
architecture.expected_effect: Earlier detection of irreversible biofouling signatures relative to the present 3-week CIP interval-driven reactive strategy, enabling targeted non-chlorine biofilm mitigation (e.g., enhanced pre-treatment biofilter backwash frequency or UV dosing adjustments) before normalized flux droop reaches 15%, supporting return toward the designed quarterly cleaning schedule without reducing permeate recovery.
architecture.falsification_test: Run the hardened 3-arm soft-sensor diagnostic in parallel with existing 2-arm diagnostics for 6 months; if normalized-flux-droop data and inline biofilm sensor readings show no statistically significant improvement in time-to-first-biofilm-diagnosis warning (no sooner than current CIP-triggering thresholds) under identical feed-water conditions, the mechanism fails.
